## What it does

A retrieval-augmented (RAG) assistant that answers customer questions about Arya Bank's savings, credit card, home loan, KYC and dispute policies, citing the policy document it used. Arya Bank is fictional; its five policy documents are the only knowledge source.

## Intended use

- Answer factual questions about published Arya Bank policies, with a citation to the source document
- Apply a published rule to a customer's stated situation (for example, which late-fee slab applies)
- Tell the customer when a question is not covered by the policy documents

## Out of scope

- Investment, tax or legal advice, or recommending one product over another
- Accessing or changing any customer account (the assistant has no tools)
- Questions about products not covered by the five policy documents
- Use without the citation shown to the customer

**Users:** Retail banking customers, through a self-service chat channel

**Human oversight:** Answers are informational. Fee disputes, fraud reports and account changes are handed to human agents through existing channels named in the policies.

## Components

| Component | Detail |
|---|---|
| Generator LLM | openai/gpt-oss-20b served by Groq (third-party API) |
| Judge LLM (evaluation only) | openai/gpt-oss-120b served by Groq |
| Embeddings | sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, run locally |
| Vector store | ChromaDB, local |
| Knowledge base | 5 fictional policy documents (SAV-001, CC-002, HL-003, KYC-004, DIS-005) |

## Evaluation

- **Dataset:** 24-case golden set — factual, reasoning, out-of-scope and safety questions
- **Method:** Deterministic checks plus LLM-as-a-judge (DeepEval faithfulness and answer relevancy)
- **Cadence:** Every push, every pull request and nightly
- **Runs on record:** 2 (2 on the approved configuration)

## Known limitations

- The golden set is small (24 cases) and hand-written; it does not cover every phrasing customers use
- The LLM judge is itself a model and can be wrong; its scores are supporting evidence, not ground truth
- Free-tier API limits can stop a run part-way; incomplete runs are treated as missing evidence
- English only; Hindi and Hinglish questions are untested

## Risk summary

| Risk | Inherent | Status | Residual |
|---|---|---|---|
| R01 Answers contain claims not supported by the policy documents (hallucination) | critical | 🟢 Mitigated | medium |
| R02 Wrong fees, rates, limits or dates quoted to customers | critical | 🟢 Mitigated | medium |
| R03 Assistant guesses answers to questions the policies do not cover | critical | 🟢 Mitigated | low |
| R04 Assistant refuses questions it should answer (unhelpful, pushes load to call centre) | medium | 🟢 Mitigated | low |
| R05 Missing or fabricated source citations | medium | 🟢 Mitigated | low |
| R06 Unsafe behaviour — investment advice, asking for OTPs, following injected instructions | critical | 🟢 Mitigated | medium |
| R07 Retriever returns the wrong policy, so the answer is built on the wrong source | high | 🟢 Mitigated | low |
| R08 Quality silently degrades after a prompt, model or data change | high | 🟢 Mitigated | low |
| R09 Third-party model is changed or retired by the provider | high | 🟢 Mitigated | low |
| R10 Personal or confidential customer data is exposed in answers | high | 🔵 Accepted | high |
